text.p: A women's 100 metres butterfly world short-course record set last month by Japan's Ayari Aoyama has been ratified by the International Amateur Swimming Federation (FINA).
Aoyama clocked 58.24 seconds in Tokyo on March 28 to beat the 58.29 set by American Misty Hyman in Quebec City on December 1 last year.
Phil Rogers enters this week's championships as holder of the men's 200 metres breaststroke world short-course record as fellow Australian Ryan Mitchell's faster time has not been ratified.
Mitchell, competing in the Australian short-course championships in Melbourne last December, clocked two minutes 7.66 seconds to better the 2:07.80 set by Rogers in the same pool on August 28, 1993.
But FINA refused to ratify the new time because Mitchell set it in a time-trial arranged for him after he had been disqualified for an incorrect touch in the heats and ruled out of the final.
